title: प्रथमोनुवाकः
samhita: या ते॑ हे॒तिर्मी॑डुष्टम॒ हस्ते॑ ब॒भूव॑ ते॒ धनुः॑ । तया॒-ऽस्मान्, वि॒श्वत॒स्त्वम॑य॒क्ष्मया॒ परि॑ब्भुज ॥
krama: या ते॒ । ते हे॒तिः । हे॒तिर्मी॑डुष्टम । मीढु॑ष्टम॒ हस्ते॑ । हस्ते॑ ब॒भूव॑ । ब॒भूव॑ ते॒ । ते धनुः॑ । धनु॒रिति॑ धनुः॑ । तया॒-ऽस्मान् । अ॒स्मान् वि॒श्वतः॑ । वि॒श्वत॒स्त्वम् । त्वम॑य॒क्ष्मया । अ॒य॒क्ष्मया॒ परि॑ । परि॑ भुज । भु॒जेति॑ भुज ॥

sayana.text: O most bountiful one (midhustama), greatest shedder of desires—that weapon (heti) of yours in the form of a sword etc., and also that bow which was in your hand; with that weapon and with that kind of bow, which is 'ayakshmaya'—not causing injury or disturbance—you protect (paribhuj) us from all sides (vishvatah), guard us entirely. (13)

bhatta_bhaskara.dhyana: Meditation on Shiva as detailed in standard commentaries.
bhatta_bhaskara.text: Now 'Ya te hetih' and the following three are in Anushtup. The Rishi and Deity are the Lord Himself. O Midhustama—'midhvan' has been explained; the greatest shedder. That weapon (heti) belonging to you, named the bow, which exists (babhuva) in your hand. 'Heti' is derived from the root 'han' (to kill/strike). With that weapon named the bow, which is 'ayakshmaya'—not a cause of disease or injury to devotees. From all causes of fear (vishvatah), you protect (paribhuj) us entirely. Guard us at all times, in all ways, and from all sins. The root 'bhuj' has a Vedic variation. Or: protect all of us (vishvatah), including sons and grandsons. Some say: 'heti' means violence; that violence performed by you, for the sake of which the bow, the means of violence, stays in your hand—protect us from that, etc., is the same. (13)

abhinava_shankara.dhyana: Meditation on Lord Maheshvara with resplendent Goddess.
abhinava_shankara.text:
Śrī Rudra Bhāṣyam                   65

---

    "Let the bow of the matted-haired one (Kapardin) be unstrung, and the quiver too be emptied of arrows. Let the arrows of his become incapable of wounding, and let his quiver be swift [but empty]."

Now, even for the arrows that have been blunted, the prayer is offered for their incapacitation: "Vijyam iti" — may the bow of Kapardin (the Lord with matted hair, who is the Supreme Lord), be vijya — without its bowstring; and may the arrow-holder (bāṇavān — one who bears arrows) also be viśalya — devoid of arrows. Even if the quiver holds shafts, there is the concern about arrows elsewhere, hence the [mantra] says: "Aneśan iti" — may the arrows of this Kapardin be incapable of wounding, having attained destruction in the form of inability to pierce (aneśan — may they fail to reach; nāśa in the optative-like usage of the Vedic [aorist]). Furthermore, may his niṣaṅghiḥ (the quiver) be āśu (swift/ready) — meaning capable only of holding the quiver but not qualified to perform the task of pulling out and discharging the arrows. Here, [the text] "Prabhuśca dhanvana" and so forth constitutes a single mantra for the teacher. The seer (ṛṣi) of this pair of [mantras] is Nārada, the metre is Anuṣṭup, and the deity is Śrī Rudra. [The dhyāna-śloka is:] "One should meditate upon Rudra, blazing like ten million rising suns, his form like a flaming fire, his limbs adorned with fearsome serpents, bearing various weapons." Through this [mantra] enemies are destroyed. Thus [ends] the twelfth [mantra].

meanings.english: Who; which; what; that which (relative pronoun forming correlative clauses)
meanings.nirukta: Yāska classifies yad among relative-correlative constructions fundamental to Vedic syntax. The relative clause structure 'yā te iṣuḥ ... tayā naḥ mṛḍaya' (which arrow of yours ... by that, be gracious to us) is a defining pattern of Vedic prayer — naming the fearsome and asking for its transformation.
meanings.vedantic: The relative pronoun 'yā/yad' in Vedic prayer introduces the item of fear which the devotee then asks the deity to make auspicious. This rhetorical structure embodies surrender — not denying the terrible but asking it to become gracious.

panini: P 1.1.27 — yad is classified as a sarvanāman (pronoun)
P 7.2.102-105 — declension paradigm for yad-śabda across genders
P 8.1.36 — ya-forms can be accent-bearing or enclitic depending on position

meanings.english: To you; your; of you; for you
meanings.nirukta: Nirukta 1.4 discusses pronoun forms. The enclitic 'te' is the natural conversational form of address in Vedic, more intimate than the full 'tubhyam' — it implies direct, personal communion with the deity.
meanings.vedantic: Here 'te' addresses Rudra as the Supreme Being directly. The repeated use throughout Śrī Rudram establishes the devotee's continuous awareness of the divine 'You' — the eternal subject who is never an object.

panini: P 8.1.22 — enclitic (anudātta) form
P 8.1.28 — replacement of tubhyam/tava
grammatical_references.case_ending: Dative / Genitive Singular (Caturthī / Ṣaṣṭhī Vibhakti, Ekavacana)

meanings.english: Missile; weapon; stroke; flame; any instrument of striking
meanings.nirukta: From √hi — 'hiyate preṣyate iti hetiḥ' (that which is impelled/sent forth). A more general term than iṣu — covers any weapon or missile. In mantra 13: 'yā te hetiḥ' — 'which weapon of yours'.
meanings.vedantic: In mantras 13 and 15, heti refers to Rudra's general weaponry — broader than the specific bow-and-arrow. 'Pari te dhanvano hetiḥ asmān vṛṇaktu viśvataḥ' — 'may the weapon of your bow avoid us from all sides'.

panini: √हि + क्तिन् (P 3.3.94) → हेति (with guṇa: i → e)

lexicographical_references.nighantu: Nighantu 2.20 — listed among āyudha-nāmāni (weapon names). Also used for 'flame/fire-weapon' in other Vedic contexts.
lexicographical_references.amara_kosha: Amarakośa 2.8.82 — हेतिः listed meaning 'āyudha' (weapon) in general sense.

meanings.english: The bountiful one; the generous giver; one who rains down gifts; the munificent
meanings.nirukta: From √mih — originally 'to rain/sprinkle'. Extended meaning: 'to shower gifts'. 'Mīḍhvān = dātā' — one who gives bountifully. The perfect participle form suggests one who has abundantly given — an established giver. Sāyaṇa: 'kāmānāṃ varṣitā' — one who rains desired things.
meanings.vedantic: Rudra as mīḍhuṣa transforms from the terrifying to the bountiful — the same deity who wields arrows also showers blessings. In mantra 13, the superlative 'mīḍhuṣṭama' (O most bountiful) is the climactic address — the peak of praising Rudra's generosity.

panini: P 3.2.107 — kvasu-pratyaya (perfect participle): मिह् + क्वसु → मीढ्वस् (with cerebral ḍh per P 8.2.32)
P 5.3.55 — superlative: mīḍhuṣ + tama → mīḍhuṣṭama (most bountiful)

meanings.nirukta: Yāska derives iṣu from √iṣ — 'iṣyate kṣipyate iti iṣuḥ' (that which is sent forth / hurled). The root √iṣ carries the dual sense of 'impelling/seeking' and 'desiring' — an arrow is that which is directed with intention toward its target. Nirukta 9.11 discusses arrow-related vocabulary.
meanings.vedantic: The arrow symbolizes Rudra's targeted grace or punishment — it never misses. In the Muṇḍaka Upaniṣad (2.2.4): 'śaram hy upāsā-niśitam sandhayīta' — the arrow (jīvātman) is sharpened by meditation and aimed at Brahman. Saluting the arrow acknowledges that even what strikes us is an instrument of divine purpose.

panini: √इष् + उ (Uṇādi 1.1) → इषु — the u-pratyaya forms the substantive noun
P 7.1.73 — declension follows u-kārānta (u-stem) paradigm: nom. इषुः, dat. इषवे, acc. इषुम्, nom.pl. इषवः
P 6.1.77 — sandhi rule for iṣu + e → iṣave
grammatical_references.case_ending: appears as इषवे (iṣave, dat. sg.), इषुः (iṣuḥ, nom. sg.), इषुम् (iṣum, acc. sg.), इषवः (iṣavaḥ, nom. pl.) across mantras

lexicographical_references.nighantu: Nighantu 2.20 — listed among āyudha-nāmāni (weapon names) alongside śara, bāṇa, sāyaka.
lexicographical_references.amara_kosha: Amarakośa 2.8.86 (Kṣatriya-varga, Āyudha) — इषुः listed as a synonym of arrow: 'iṣuḥ śaraś ca bāṇaś ca' — iṣu, śara, and bāṇa are synonyms for arrow.

meanings.english: To become; to be; to arise; to exist; to happen
meanings.nirukta: Nirukta 2.1 — Yāska establishes √bhū as the root of all becoming. 'Bhavati' denotes coming-into-being, while 'babhūva' (perfect) indicates accomplished/established existence. The Nirukta treats bhū as the most productive root in the language.
meanings.vedantic: In Vedānta, √bhū represents the principle of manifestation — Brahman becoming the world. 'Babhūva te dhanuḥ' — 'your bow has become [auspicious]' — represents the transformation of the terrible into the benign through prayer.

panini: P 3.2.115 — liṭ lakāra (perfect): भू → ब + भू + व → बभूव (with reduplication per P 6.1.8)
P 3.4.87 — loṭ lakāra (imperative): भू + हि → भव (with guṇa per P 7.3.84)
P 3.2.107 — past participle: भू + क्त → भूत
P 3.3.18 — verbal noun formation: भू + क्तिन् → भूतिः (prosperity)

lexicographical_references.nighantu: Nighantu 1.1 — √bhū listed among the most fundamental sattā-vācaka dhātus (existence-denoting roots).
lexicographical_references.amara_kosha: Amarakośa 3.3.213 — भूतम् (past participle) listed meaning 'prāpta' (obtained) and 'jāta' (born). भूतानि as 'beings' appears in Amarakośa 1.1.7.

meanings.nirukta: Yāska connects dhanvan to √dhan (to produce sound) — the bow is characterized by its resonant twang when released. Also related to √dhanv (to curve/run) — its arc shape. Nirukta 9.11 notes the relationship between the bow's curve and the concept of all-pervading reach.
meanings.vedantic: Muṇḍaka Upaniṣad (2.2.4): 'dhanur gṛhītvā aupaniṣadaṃ mahāstram' — 'Taking up the great weapon, the bow of the Upaniṣads' — the bow is Oṃkāra (Praṇava). It is both the vehicle of destruction and liberation. In Śrī Rudram context, saluting the bow acknowledges the instrument through which divine will operates.

panini: √धन् + वनिप् (Uṇādi 4.113) → धन्वन् — vanip-pratyaya forms the n-stem noun
P 7.1.75 — an-anta (n-stem) declension paradigm: nom. धनुः (with P 8.2.7 n → anusvāra → ḥ), dat. धन्वने
P 6.4.8 — sarvanāmasthāna rules for the alternation between dhanvan-/dhanus- stems
P 8.2.7 — conversion of final n to visarjanīya in nom. sg.: dhanvans → dhanuḥ

lexicographical_references.nighantu: Nighantu 2.20 — listed among āyudha-nāmāni (weapon names). The Naighaṇṭuka tradition pairs it with iṣu as the primary weapon-set.
lexicographical_references.amara_kosha: Amarakośa 2.8.85 (Kṣatriya-varga, Āyudha) — 'dhanuḥ koḍaṇḍam' — dhanus and koḍaṇḍa are synonyms for bow. Also 'cāpaḥ śarāsanam' as further synonyms.

meanings.nirukta: Functions as the correlative partner to yad (relative pronoun). The construction 'yā te iṣuḥ ... tayā naḥ mṛḍaya' uses yā...tayā as relative-correlative pair.
meanings.vedantic: In Vedāntic usage, 'tad' famously refers to Brahman — 'tat tvam asi' (Chāndogya 6.8.7). The correlative use here points to the identity between the terrible and the auspicious.

panini: P 1.1.27 — tad classified as sarvanāman
P 7.2.102 — declension paradigm for tad-śabda
P 7.1.25 — suppletion: nom. sg. masc. becomes saḥ (not tadaḥ)

meanings.english: Us; to us; our; from us (first person plural)
meanings.nirukta: The first person plural establishes the communal nature of Vedic prayer — the ṛṣi speaks not for himself alone but for the community.
meanings.vedantic: The shift from 'te' (you) to 'naḥ' (us) establishes the devotee-deity relationship. In Advaita, the apparent duality of 'you' and 'us' is ultimately resolved in the identity of Ātman and Brahman.

panini: P 8.1.22 — नः is the enclitic form, governed by same pragraha rules as ते
P 7.2.97 — accusative plural: अस्मान्
P 7.2.86 — ablative: अस्मत्

meanings.english: All; entire; universal; every; the whole; from all sides (as viśvataḥ)
meanings.nirukta: From √viś — 'viśati prāpnoti sarvam iti viśvam' (that which enters/pervades everything). Viśva denotes totality in an all-pervading sense.
meanings.vedantic: In mantra 8: 'viśvā bhūtāni' — 'all beings'. The entire manifest creation sees Rudra-as-sun. Viśvataḥ (from all sides) in mantras 13 and 15 emphasizes comprehensive protection — Rudra's grace covers all directions.

panini: P 1.1.27 — viśva classified as sarvanāman
P 5.3.7 — tasil-pratyaya: viśva + tas → viśvatas (from all sides)

lexicographical_references.amara_kosha: Amarakośa 3.1.1 — विश्वम् listed as synonym of sarva: 'sarvaḥ viśvaḥ'.

meanings.nirukta: Ubha denotes 'both together' — always used in dual. In mantra 14: 'ubhābhyām uta te namaḥ' — 'to both [arms], and to you, salutation'. In mantra 10: 'ubhayoḥ ārtniyoḥ' — 'from both bow-tips'.
meanings.vedantic: The dual 'both' emphasizes the completeness of the salutation — both arms, both ends of the bow. Nothing is left unacknowledged.

panini: P 1.1.27 — ubha classified as sarvanāman
P 7.1.55 — ubha used only in dual forms

meanings.english: Free from disease; healthy; without consumption/wasting; without affliction
meanings.nirukta: Yakṣma is a general term for wasting disease (consumption/tuberculosis in later medical texts). Ayakṣma = absence of such disease. In Vedic context, yakṣma encompasses all debilitating illness — 'yat kṣīṇaṃ bhavati tat yakṣma' (that which causes wasting is yakṣma).
meanings.vedantic: In mantra 5: 'ayakṣmaṃ sumanā asat' — 'may [the world] be free from disease and of good mind'. Health of body (ayakṣma) and mind (sumanās) together constitute well-being. In Vedānta, the ultimate yakṣma is avidyā (ignorance) — freedom from spiritual disease is mokṣa.

panini: P 6.2.155 — nañ-tatpuruṣa: a + yakṣma → ayakṣma
P 2.2.6 — negative compound formation

lexicographical_references.nighantu: Nighantu 2.9 — yakṣma listed among roga-vācaka (disease-denoting) words. Ayakṣma is its negation.

meanings.english: Protect all around; embrace; shelter on every side; wrap around protectively
meanings.nirukta: Compound verb: pari (all around) + √bhuj (to protect/bend). 'Pari-bhuja' = 'shelter us on all sides'. Sāyaṇa: 'sarvataḥ pālaya' (protect from every direction). In mantra 13: 'ayakṣmayā pari bhuja' — 'with [your] disease-free [grace], protect us all around'.
meanings.vedantic: The final plea in mantra 13 asks for complete, all-encompassing protection (pari = all around). The adverb viśvataḥ (from all sides) reinforces this. Rudra's protection is not partial but total — the devotee is wrapped in divine grace from every direction.

panini: P 3.4.87 — loṭ: परि + भुज् + हि → परिभुज

meanings.nirukta: From √bhuj (to protect / preserve / enjoy). Pari-bhuja: protect us completely from all sides.
meanings.vedantic: The core prayer asking Lord Shiva to encompass and protect the seeker on all sides.

grammatical_references.panini: Root √bhuj + Lot (imperative) 2nd person singular active → bhuja.
